#4283. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4279. 10 Legendary Grenades and Ordnances You Should Have in Borderlands 4

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

There are various types of legendary items in Borderlands 4, and it goes without saying that they are some of the best items in the game. Because of this, you will want to fill your endgame build with legendary items galore.

The main items you will be using across your builds are weapons, shields, and grenades. Once you have some powerful legendary weapons and have acquired a shield, you will need to focus on getting either a strong grenade or a strong ordnance. For a primary weapon, consider the best legendary assault rifles.

There are numerous legendary grenades and ordnances in Borderlands 4, and several of them are must-have items at this point in the game to refine your build with.

There are some grenades that you have to be careful about where you throw them, and then there are grenades that many refer to as “throw and forget” grenades. This is because you don’t need to worry about where you throw them. Instead, you can toss it in a general direction and go.

The Swarm is a grenade you can forget about because it homes in on targets. Its ability, Swoosh, makes it spawn three homing grenades on impact, and those spawn additional homing grenades for a total of nine.

If you happen to get bonuses on this build that increase your grenade damage and explosion size, you will be living the dream. You can get the Swarm from Sidney Pointylegs in Hungering Plain.

If you are someone who wants to use ordnances, your options are somewhat limited, as there aren’t as many of them in the game, but they are quite powerful. One of the more powerful ones is the Disc Jockey.

This heavy launcher has the ability Bouncing Biscuits, which makes it so it launches energy discs that bounce off surfaces. Each time one of these discs bounces, the damage of the disc increases by 20%.

This is a weapon that is great in small rooms, as the bounces can rack up some serious damage on groups of enemies. You can get this weapon from Sidney Pointylegs in Hungering Plain.

It is interesting whenever a grenade doesn’t deal grenade damage and instead gets all its power from another source. In the case of the Barb’ara, it gets its damage from your skill damage buffs, making it perfect for those who are running skill builds.

This grenade has the ability Tentacles, which causes it to create a tentacle explosion on impact. The explosion created by this impact deals skill damage. These tentacles will spawn two additional grenades that create more tentacles, also dealing skill damage.

Since every Vault Hunter in the game can run a skill build, this is a great grenade to have whenever you decide to switch up your build. You can farm this grenade from Crazed Earl in the Vault of the Damned DLC.

There are plenty of weapons in Borderlands 4 that have been added in DLC. Which ones of them are the best?

Sometimes you just want to fire a rocket launcher and let it delete your problems. In this case, the problem is usually a group of enemies or a massive boss that is blocking your path. The Loiter Sploiter is designed to take care of these problems quickly, and is great if you have an ordnance-focused build and amp gear.

The Loiter Sploiter’s ability, Sploiter, makes it so this weapon fires high-damage rockets. These rockets then spawn additional rockets when they explode, causing massive amounts of damage.

If you are running gear with the amped ability, this will power up these rockets, making them capable of one-shotting bosses with ease. You can get this weapon Infamous Dave in the Murders & Acquisitions DLC.

There are some grenades in Borderlands 4 that don’t just explode. Instead, they have some quirky effects such as shooting lasers or a machine gun at enemies before they explode. Either way, you get an explosion.

The Alignment is one of those grenades, as it has the ability Coordinated, which makes it so the grenade seeks out an enemy when thrown, hovers above them, shoots them with a beam of elemental energy, and then divebombs them.

It is an interesting effect that makes that weapon great for dealing elemental status effects, and therefore, is good for those who want an elemental status effect build. You can obtain this grenade from the Warped & Weird Vault Card.

Speaking of the weird and quirky, the Heimdahl is perhaps the weirdest of the ordnance weapons in Borderlands 4. This is because the weapon shoots Dahl soldier heads that attack enemies. They are out for revenge, and will kill anyone in their way.

The ability of this weapon is called Rig. It fires soldier heads that fly around the battlefield, track down enemies, and vomit on them. This deals significant damage, and is a weapon that you can fire and forget since it tracks enemies.

This weapon is perfect for Vault Hunter builds where you don’t need to worry about ordnance ammo, as you can just keep firing it and clear out a room in no time. You can obtain this weapon from Captain Willis in The Maelstrom in the Vault of the Damned DLC.

There are plenty of legendary assault rifles in Borderlands 4, and we will show you how to get them all.

The Blockbuster grenade is one that will clear an area with ease, but you better make sure to stay out of the area or you will get killed. This grenade is designed to do one thing, which is to cause numerous explosions.

The ability of this grenade is called Got You Covered, and it does give you plenty of cover. This ability makes the grenade split into four grenades on impact. These grenades then spawn an additional two grenades. This sounds normal until you realize that these grenades all bounce in place, creating explosions as they do.

It will cover the field in explosions, and you just need to stay out of the way so you don’t get killed. You can get this grenade from Vile Lictor in Terminus Range.

The Firepot is similar to the Swarm grenade, but it focuses on dealing fire damage and it loves to stick grenades to enemies. Torgue returns with one of the finest grenades in Borderlands 4, and it packs a serious punch.

The ability of this grenade is called Spicy, and it makes the grenade spawn homing Torgue sticky grenades that attach to enemies. In total, nine grenades will spawn from this bad boy, and they will each explode after 13 seconds, igniting the enemies that are unfortunate enough to be hit by them.

It is another throw and forget style grenade that does an amazing job covering the field without you needing to focus too much on what you are doing. You can get this grenade from Leader Willem in Grindstone of the Worthy.

The Waterfall was one of my first legendary grenades in Borderlands 4, so it holds a special place in my heart, and it might be a bit weaker than some of the other weapons on this list. However, this doesn’t mean that it isn’t worth getting, as it packs a serious punch.

This grenade has the Waterfall ability, which makes it explode multiple times whenever it hits an enemy. Throw it in a group, and each enemy damaged by the grenade will cause another explosion, cascading the damage over the surrounding area.

It can wipe out groups of enemies easily, but it is noticeably not as effective as the Swarm. You can get this grenade by farming Bio-Bulkhead in the Dissected Plateau.

There are some grenades and ordnances that can clear out entire rooms, and then there are some that are focused on one thing, and that is killing bosses. The Draupner is basically a delete button for life’s problems, and it is amazing.

Return Wave is the name of the Draupner’s ability, and it makes the weapon fire out three saw blades in a horizontal pattern from the weapon. These saw blades return to you after two seconds or upon impact, effectively hitting enemies twice over.

This ordnance effectively diminishes the damage numbers of every other ordnance in the game, making it a must-have weapon. You can obtain it by running the Takedown at the Hadron Abyss.

There are plenty of legendary weapons in Borderlands 4, but these are the weapons that you should have at this point if you want a strong build.

#4276. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Have you ever thought about the various types of Pokémon out there? There are some that are quite terrifying. After all, some of them are sharks, others are literal dragons, and there are even Pokémon gods.

Living in the world of Pokémon, you need to be able to defend yourself, and instead of using another Pokémon to fight your battles, you need to start throwing hands. So, I pose the question, “What Pokémon do you think you could take in a fist fight?”

Do you think you are able to beat up an Eevee? Maybe you could take down an Arcanine. Here are some Pokémon you would definitely stand a chance against.

Hear me out, but I think we could all easily take a Ditto in a fight. It has the ability Transform, but in battle, it only transforms into what it is currently fighting. Therefore, the Ditto would transform into you.

Do you think you could take yourself in a fight? I certainly think I could take myself in a fight. It wouldn’t be the easiest battle, but it is certainly better than dealing with a fox that can breathe fire or a mouse that can electrocute you.

You know your strengths and weaknesses, and so all you really need to do is use that to your advantage. Ditto doesn’t know anything about your weaknesses, so you have an advantage.

If it wasn’t obvious, Komala is based on the Koala Bear, and its Pokédex entries make it out to be one in the same. It eats poison leaves that only it can digest. This makes it tired, and it continuously sleeps.

It is said that Komala is asleep from the time it is born to when it dies, and that all of its movements are based on dreams that it is having. This makes it a prime target, and a Pokémon that you could easily take in a fight.

The only issue you may have while fighting this Pokémon is that it will thrash about wildly if you remove the log it is holding. Just don’t mess with its log and you will be fine. It will just think the fight was a dream.

Spoink is an adorable little Pokémon that nobody would ever hurt, but if it came at you looking to fight, you could easily take it. Its Pokédex reveals your entire plan of action, as it states that it needs to keep bouncing in order for its heart to keep beating.

All you need to do is knock it over. It might give you some trouble with its bouncing, but if you can get ahold of its tail, all you need to do is get its back to the ground and its heart will stop.

That is pretty grim, but you have to remember that it is survival of the fittest out there, and Spoink is one of those Pokémon that can easily be defeated with little prep time and some strong actions.

Pokemon isn't all about types and stats. With the right strategy and a bit of training, any Pokemon can be a force to be reckoned with.

Slowpoke is constantly the butt of the joke when it comes to the Pokémon being slow. Its reaction timing is so poor that you could probably land 20 punches before it even realizes what is going on.

Think about it. In the games, people eat Slowpoke tails. It is so common that there are even restaurants in Lumiose City that sell it for dinner every night.

I can only take that as a sign that Slowpoke is easily defeated and captured. How else would they be able to get so many of those tails? After all, you wouldn’t be able to do the same to a Pokémon like Totodile. It would immediately bite your face off.

Sudowoodo would be a terrifying Pokémon to fight, but its pre-evolution, Bonsly, would be an easy victory. Bonsly isn’t much of a fighter, preferring to rest for hours in arid climates.

Enemies don’t typically attack Bonsly because it exudes moisture from its eyes that look like tears. However, we can see through this deception, and that makes us a difficult foe for this Pokémon.

It is said that Bonsly can easily be defeated if it gets too wet, so all you really need to do is dump a bucket of water on it and it is done for. You just need to have no empathy while dealing with this Pokémon or you won’t be able to finish the job.

Some Pokémon are tiny and have barely any defense mechanisms. One such Pokémon is Caterpie. While it may be a cute bug, it is also a bug that you could easily take in a fight.

The only real issue here is that it has a defense mechanism that allows it to release a horrifically foul odor from its body, but if you bring some nose plugs, you will be perfectly fine. Maybe fight it while wearing a gas mask just to be safe.

Other than that, you don’t have to worry about anything from this Pokémon. It has a massive appetite for leaves, so all you really need to do is wait for it to start eating and jump it. Everything will be fine unless you are afraid of them like Misty is.

Milcery is a strange Pokémon, as its body is literally cream. Its Pokédex entry says that it is born from “sweet-smelling particles.” These particles condense into a cream that forms Milcery’s body.

Well, if Milcery is made of cream, that means you just need to eat your way to victory. That sounds like a simple victory to me.

The Pokédex entries give an idea about how this Pokémon fights. It says that Milcery just covers attackers in cream and runs away. In other words, find a way not to get blinded by cream, and you will have no problem taking this Pokémon out. You will even have desert for later.

This list covers the worst Pokémon from generations 1 through 9, and why they fail to capture the attention of players.

Fidough is adorable, there is no denying that one, but it also wouldn’t be difficult to take it in a fight. All it is known for, according to the Pokédex, is producing yeast with its breath to help baked goods rise.

It is also dependent on humans. One of the Pokédex entries says that it has been protected by humans for generations, so it probably doesn’t know how to defend itself without the help of a human companion.

Plus, its short and stubby legs are a bit of a disadvantage. This is a fight that you could easily win. Now, it might be a completely different conversation when Dachsbun is involved, but luckily, we are just talking about Fidough here.

You might see me calling Magikarp weak and pathetic and think that I am just being cruel, but believe me, I am only following what the Pokédex says. Some of the early Pokédex entries say that Magikarp is a weak and pathetic Pokémon that only flops about.

Magikarp is known for getting easily pushed around. It may have some tough scales, but all you need to do is bring a slightly strong weapon and you are golden. Maybe a few kicks would be enough.

During the fight, it will only splash about. Just watch for when it hits seven feet in the air, because that is the height limit for it. You may think the water would save it, but there are so many of them, you are bound to catch one easily.

There are some very weak Pokémon in the games and anime. For instance, Wishiwashi is very weak in its solo form, but I don’t feel like fishing for hours or jumping into the water. However, Sunkern doesn’t have that issue and it is also one of the weakest Pokémon in the game.

With 30 points in each stat and a base stat total of 180, it is amazing that Sunkern can even survive a single battle against any Pokémon. To further show how weak it is, its Pokédex entry says that it tries to move as little as possible to conserve energy.

With how little Sunkern likes to move and how weak it is, I bet anyone could take it in a fight. I’d be shocked if anyone lost to this Pokémon.

From Ultra Necrozma’s stat boosts to Volo’s grueling final battle, these Pokémon encounters bend the rules to deliver memorable challenges.

#4271. Poll: Will You Be Using Zelda Notes With Ocarina Of Time?

With the Ocarina of Time Switch 2 remake, Nintendo is once again using its Zelda Notes feature via the Nintendo Switch app for mobile.

While I wasn't able to access and test out the app's features during the review period, I've been dabbling quite a bit since Nintendo pushed it live for launch. And y'know what? It's fine.

Just like Zelda Notes for Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom, there's nothing here that I'd deem essential to the core experience, but if you're after some harmless supplemental material, it does the job.

My favourite feature? Gossip Quests. Provided you've activated Zelda Notes within Ocarina of Time's settings, you can link your phone directly to the software to partake in a little game to hunt down specific locations depicted in photos. Doing so will earn you points, which you can eventually spend on new ocarina songs.

To be clear, these ocarina songs won't unlock anything in-game, but you can access a playable ocarina in the app and learn the songs yourself, tapping and holding the on-screen holes to perform a variety of tunes.

It's surprisingly tricky, and in an amusing turn of events, pressing three holes at once also acted as a screenshot tool for my phone, so I had to go ahead and delete that function in my phone settings.

You can also come up with your own, original songs and share them via QR code. I haven't come up with anything I'd deem even remotely enjoyable for anyone else, but it's a cool little feature. [For the authentic Ocarina experience circa 1998, I need The Simpsons theme, stat! - Ed.]

Once unlocked in the game, you can also view enemies from the Hall of Fallen Foes. The app also provides a wealth of stats, including daily records, and you can also consult maps if you're gunning for 100% completion and test your Ocarina of Time knowledge with quizzes.

Again, it's fine. There are features, like the Gossip Quests, that would have been awesome had they been included in the game itself in some way, and we'd recommend at least giving it a go if you're looking to extend your playtime. (Fingers crossed for a Master Quest update!)

Let us know if you plan on using the Zelda Notes app by voting in the below polls:

Leave a comment and let us know how much (if at all) you've used Zelda Notes so far.

#4270. Battlefield 6’s first big map in months is coming to Labs soon, but I'm more excited about BF4's Golmud Railway making its way to BF6

As promised, Battlefield Labs is coming back to bring us a preview of some of Battlefield 6’s upcoming Season 2 content.

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off new gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

For context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios says it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

#4269. The Elder Scrolls VI Has An Official Subtitle And It's 'Sentinel'

The headline tells the story: The Elder Scrolls VI has an official subtitle and it's Sentinel. So the full game is now titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, or, as we will undoubtedly refer to it moving forward, as we colloquially do with the previous three games (Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim), Sentinel.

The news comes from Bethesda's various social media accounts, which are all sharing the video above. Along with the video, music, and the title, it also shares the text as a quote attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest to High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell (4E 206): "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."

Sentinel is one of the nine major kingdoms within Hammerfell and is the capital of both the Alik'r Desert region and the Myrkwasa region of the Alik'r (source: elderscrolls.fandom). With this knowledge, it's fair to assume Sentinel will have many desert locations.

The name continues the tradition of naming the games after locations in the Elder Scrolls universe. Oblivion is the sort of exception, as it is a realm, but it still counts. We still don't know exactly when The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel will be released, but we're now about seven years from its original announcement at E3 2018.

#4268. Arc Raiders finally reveals early 2026 roadmap, but we’re not getting a new map for a while

The first couple of months of 2026 in the world of Arc Raiders look pretty promising, but the big guns are being held back for now.

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a new matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a new Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map update during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

#4267. 7 Video Games That Could Sweep in The Game Awards, Ranked

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

Winter holidays bring joy through family gatherings and discounted video games, but they have also become synonymous with awards ceremonies celebrating the year's finest releases.

In the case at hand, 2026 has established itself as a magnificent trip around the sun thanks to the numerous masterful titles that have been, or will be, released during its 12 months, making for a fiercely contested race to see which is the best.

The number of events held for this purpose is as vast as it is diverse, although all eyes are on December 10th, the day the interactive industry's Ballon d'Or is awarded.

Therefore, if you're as eager as I am to see if any video game can come close to Clair Obscur: Expedition 33's phenomenal success last year, I recommend you read this list of seven video games that could sweep The Game Awards, ranked.

The first and most underrated video game to appear on this list is none other than Big Walk, a game that will arrive completely silent despite having the power to surprise more than a few on this special night.

That it will win Best Multiplayer should be a given, but this would be merely the bare minimum of the recognition that House House's team has earned through one of the most special and creative indie games of recent years.

Because of this, and considering it's this year's highest-rated game on Metacritic if we don't count remasters and remakes, there's more than enough reason to believe it could become 2026's most acclaimed independent production.

My bets for Game Direction and Audio Design are bolder, especially since these are usually awarded to larger projects with bigger budgets. However, given what happened last year, I wouldn't rule out Big Walk silencing more than a few detractors.

This article ranks the Game of the Year nominee classes from The Game Awards each year of the 2020s.

A particularly curious case is that of Control Resonant, which presents itself as a solid piece in numerous departments, even though I don't believe its overall acclaim is sufficient to be a Game of the Year contender.

Said detail aside, Remedy knows what it's like to have a string of successes after Alan Wake 2 won three of its eight nominations in 2023, and its latest project could repeat that feat with even greater force.

Specifically, in terms of the audiovisual component, it's by far one of the year's strongest contenders, which hasn't stood out for its narratives or art direction at Control Resonant's level, except in the indie scene.

That a title can win so many awards without being Game of the Year already happened in 2022 with God of War: Ragnarök, and for reasons very similar to those experienced by Kratos's latest adventure, I think we could be facing the same scenario now.

Capcom has been, arguably by a wide margin, the most outstanding developer of the year, having released Monster Hunter Stories 3, Pragmata, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and, most relevantly for this occasion, Resident Evil: Requiem.

Angela Sant'Albano's stellar performance as Grace Ashcroft already guarantees a strong chance of winning an award despite the fierce competition, as does its status as the best horror game of the year and all that entails in terms of gameplay and audio design.

From there, Resident Evil: Requiem faces an uphill battle to win all the awards for which it will surely be a candidate, as it is undeniably one of the best games of the year.

Will being the best Resident Evil be enough to secure every possible nomination? Time will tell, but its candidacy and the seriousness with which it must be approached can be anticipated from this very moment.

The Game Awards has six awesome titles up for Game Of The Year in 2025, but here are seven more that still feel like they've been snubbed.

The Game Awards' biggest winners last year ranged from indie to AA titles, opening up a world of possibilities for this and future iterations, especially for extraordinary adventures like Mina the Hollower.

The current lineup isn't as fertile for indie products to take center stage as it did in 2025, but I'm certain that, if any prospect can truly achieve that, it's Yacht Club Games' masterpiece.

As for Best Indie Game, Best Action-Adventure Game, and Game Direction, I'd bet my life that this wonderful ode to classic video games will be in the running, aiming to take home those awards, though it's outstanding enough in the other categories to warrant consideration as well.

The interactive medium's pendulum is increasingly swinging in favor of indie games in these turbulent times, where the biggest companies keep making bad decisions, so Mina the Hollower could capitalize on those protest votes.

The year's not-so-surprise surprise is Phantom Blade Zero, which stands on the shoulders of Black Myth: Wukong to likely become the Chinese video game with the most nominations and prizes at The Game Awards.

As part of the top three contenders for the People's Choice Award, I see S-Game's gem as a work robust enough to compete with the two titans that you and I both know round out this list, which says everything you need to know about its quality.

Its greatest strength is its unique character, stemming from a singular design, composition, and presentation philosophy that we've seen only a handful of times, allowing it to stand out with literally unparalleled ease and fluidity among the rest.

It has more than enough quality to win any title it's given, so much so that, if we were in any other year of the decade, I could easily predict that Phantom Blade Zero would be GOTY.

The Best Games For Impact Nominees Of All Time are emotional and thought-provoking experiences.

Nevertheless, the year is 2026, and it just so happens that it coincides with the return of what many consider the best video game of all time, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake.

If there's one reason why I feel most action-adventure games will have a tough time, it's because the quintessential adventure has returned, the one that paved the way for the entire genre in the three decades following its release.

From the music to its underrated art direction, including its technical and gameplay splendor, it's safe to say that the Ocarina of Time remake will be present even in the Muppet segments created by the legendary Geoff Keighley.

In 1998, there was no The Game Awards to give Link's odyssey the recognition it deserved, so don't be surprised if the video game industry, as a whole, makes this year the perfect moment to rectify that omission.

If we take into account what its immediate predecessor did and what its creators have promised to do with it, there's no doubt that the top contender to sweep The Game Awards is Grand Theft Auto 6.

Rockstar is fully aware that, every year they release a game, December becomes a month of metaphorical and material praise, given their habit of releasing the most ambitious and massive titles the industry is ready to see.

Link is a formidable competitor, and that's indisputable, yet Lucia and Jason have the added momentum of being the most anticipated video game in history and the most expensive ever made, making them immediate candidates for a third of the event's categories.

It's difficult to predict with certainty, though if there's one thing I can be partially sure of, it's that Ocarina of Time and GTA 6 will quickly make this article obsolete by taking home practically every award between them.

These titles were left at the gates of glory, but they deserved to be called Game of the Year.

#4266. Nioh 3’s generous demo is out now, and your progress carries over to the full game

If you’re looking for a way to check out one of the biggest releases of early 2026, Team Ninja has made it easy for you.

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

More specifically, preloading on Xbox Series X/S will begin Tuesday, November 10, at 12 a.m. GMT (4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on November 9), and on PS5 at midnight local time in your time zone. #4264. How Long Does It Take To Finish The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake?

The time has finally come to return to one of Nintendo's best games, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, with a brand-new look and streamlined gameplay. Though players who have played the original will undoubtedly have an advantage over those who haven't, the remake also makes it much easier for new players to navigate the world.

With all that said, while new players won't spend quite as much time on the remake as they might have if they were playing the original for the first time, the game is still paced to ensure you enjoy the journey.

As mentioned, the time it takes you to beat the Ocarina of Time remake largely depends on whether you've played the original and whether you're planning to 100 percent the game. If you are playing Ocarina of Time for the first time, ever, then you should expect to spend around 22–25 hours on the game's main story.

If you've played the original Ocarina of Time, you likely already know where to go and what you're looking for, meaning you will spend less time wandering than new players. So, your completion time should be closer to 18–20 hours. The small range factors in the fact that returning players are also likely to explore a bit to see all the changes and enjoy the new graphics.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Switch 2 remake had a young development team, and they were told to ignore the Zelda timeline.

Of course, whether you've played the game before or not, reaching 100 percent completion in Ocarina of Time will take some time. Most collectibles are in the same general area as the original, but a few things have been moved around enough that new players will also need to do some searching. Not to mention, unless you played the original recently, you've likely forgotten the original locations anyway.

With all that said, if you're looking to 100-percent finish Ocarina of Time, you should expect to spend closer to 30 hours on the game. You can save yourself some time by being as thorough as possible the first time you pass through a new area or dungeon, but either way, you should expect to add somewhere between 8–10 hours to your standard story completion time.

We finally got a chance to play The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and it's still one of the best games ever made.

Here are the start and end times for the second Spellcasters Chronicles closed beta, as well as what's new in this latest test.

Quantic Dream has opened up its upcoming fantasy MOBA for a second closed beta weekend starting from today, January 29, until 9AM UTC on Monday February 2.

The closed beta is for PC only in Europe, Asia and North America and potential players can register to join the waitlist for a key at the game’s official website or on the Spellcasters Chronicles Steam page. Players who had access to the first closed beta will automatically have access to the second, but you can sign up on both the site and Steam to increase your chances of entry.

The MOBA genre is competitive in every sense and Quantic Dream is trying to break into it with a Magic the Gathering-esque spin on the format. Players build a deck of cards before queuing into teams of 3, then face off as battling mages, summoning creatures, building fortifications and casting spells rather than choosing a Hero with unique abilities in the traditional MOBA style.

Beta content includes a new map, 6 new spells and 5 new summon creatures for your deck, as well as 3 new buildings too.

Also new for this second closed beta is an introduction and tutorial for some of the game’s finer details, as well as a text chat for strategising and much-needed player reporting system to go with it. It will also feature early versions of the Spellcaster customisation system and ranked matches.

#4261. Afterwords – Marvel’s Wolverine

We interviewed game director Mike Daly after the launch of Insomniac’s recent Wolverine game to get his take on what makes Wolverine and Spidey different to work on, his thoughts on breadcrumb trails, and why Logan can’t ever seem to get the girl.

Insomniac had extensive experience working on well-known superhero characters before starting on Wolverine. Early on, what traits or qualities of Logan as a story character and playable avatar did you know you wanted to focus on, distinct from the Spider-Man games and character?

From a story perspective, we wanted Logan to be a man with centuries of experiences that he can’t remember, creating a mix of being worn, wizened, and cynical. His resilience makes him fearless, which comes through in his candid manner, and he can’t ignore his sense of justice, as much as he would like to.

For gameplay, it was important that players felt the difference made by his healing factor, claws, berserker rage, animalistic strength, enhanced senses, his adamantium skeleton, and corresponding weight.

In both story and gameplay, emotionally and physically, Wolverine is a hero who gets hurt and feels that pain deeply but always gets back up again and presses on. This dogged resilience was really important to us and a central theme of story and gameplay.

Wolverine is more of a linear adventure than the open-world exploration of a big city seen in Spidey. In my playthrough, that added to the sense of relentless pacing that characterizes Wolverine as a fictional lead. Was that part of the thinking behind why the game was built that way, or was the more linear path there for other reasons?

Ultimately, we made a game suited for a Wolverine story that had comic book pacing – action and meaningful story development on every page.

We experimented with different structures and stories, evaluating from the perspective of: “Is this the best way to do Wolverine justice?” As the various things we tried didn’t feel right, we had to challenge our assumptions and look to our favorite Wolverine stories for inspiration, which led us to where we ended up – a story with momentum in which every beat felt authentic to the character.

Scenes and gameplay sequences that might have been fine in other games but didn’t strongly evoke Wolverine undermined the consistency of the fantasy we were trying to create, so we tried to keep things very focused.

After the game’s release, there was an active online conversation about some of the breadcrumb-trail guidance the game offers to lead you to pickups, or to mark the continued golden path of progression. What was the thinking internally about that design decision, and your take on the debate after the game launched?

Our thinking was that it was essential to make the player feel like they were empowered by Logan’s enhanced senses, a canonical mutant ability, enabling players to do things they could not with other characters. We wanted to weave that power into as many parts of the game as we could, so that if Logan could smell or hear something relevant, the player could see it too.

For collectibles, we wanted players to enjoy seeking out and spotting senses cues, enabling you to find things that would have been obscure to other characters. Using the cues, players can cover a lot of ground without feeling the need to scour, maintaining story and action momentum.

After the game launched, we saw feedback from players that interpreted senses as abstract designer guidance, along with a desire for options in how they approached exploration and discovery. Fortunately, we have been able to incorporate this feedback from players in our post-launch patches. One aspect we’ve improved is the scent trail’s organic presentation, so they give a stronger impression that they belong in the world rather than being an abstraction. For players that want to do more manual exploration, we’ve added options to remove the sense cues for optional collectibles, and one to make scent trails dimmer until the player requests a hint.

Ultimately, enhanced senses are still essential to creating an authentic Wolverine, and that’s still reflected in the cinematic and environmental storytelling of the game. I think it’s great that on top of that, players now have more flexibility in how they experience them.

As a longtime comics fan, I found Logan’s combat system especially exciting, particularly for the relentless forward momentum it provided. What do you think were some of the keys to nailing that dynamic, as distinct from other high-quality third-person action games?

There were a few key elements we wanted to get right - Logan’s resilience, rage, claw feel, and overall lethality.

For resilience, Logan’s healing factor needed to feel important for survival - a prominent element of the system. A natural starting point there was to try continual regeneration so you could outlast enemies, but that quickly fell apart as it incentivized the player to slow the pace of combat or even retreat for maximum advantage. Even though it was incredibly effective at enabling survival, it was also hard to notice by the player so it didn’t feel prominent.

The key to solving this problem was making a connection between rage and healing factor. The Last Stand mechanic is a healing surge that can happen when you lose all your health, themed as using adrenaline to keep Logan’s heart beating. This incentivized aggression and made a space for an up-close look at visceral healing.

Speaking of rage, it’s the backbone of the combat system where being an indicator of momentum is key. At the low end of rage, you don’t have the safety net of Last Stand, so your decision-making naturally biases towards survival; ensuring you prioritize threat assessment and defense. As you climb into the middle tier, you have the leeway to push your luck for longer combos or barrages that let you build up rage and get kills faster. Finally, you get to rage tier 3, where the quick decay of rage makes your rate of kills the top priority, so you might prefer to attack groups over ranged stragglers just for the improved kill density. Beyond the mechanics, we change the presentation of combat, especially through Logan’s animations and exertion to reflect his state of mind. The presentation and systemic incentives drive the player into a frenzy, just like Wolverine.

We invested a lot in the details of claw feel to make sure it was distinct from general game attacks. Claws shred, so we added locational body damage to our enemies to reflect that, along with a dynamic blood system where it globs together as it is spilled, splatters on contact with characters or the environment, drips down the walls, diffuses in the water, and other details. Many kills throughout combat are punctuated with custom animations with cinematic camera work that pushes in and frames the puncturing of claws into the body for a strong impression of the connection and weight of the puncture. Severing limbs on these attacks is an occasional reminder of how sharp Logan’s adamantium claws are. Reinforcing this is top-notch sound and haptics design, so each hit registers.

The last aspect I’ll touch on is lethality, the rate at which Wolverine is able to dispatch enemies and vice versa. We found that fights where enemies were more technical and could survive a lot undermined what players expected to experience as Wolverine, which was aggressively and lethally tearing through a lot of enemies. On the other hand, combat was less exciting if the enemies didn’t feel like a serious and deadly threat, and you didn’t feel like Wolverine if a little bit of caution could enable you to defend perfectly and avoid all damage.

These aspects led us towards encounters where you confronted large groups of enemies that were highly aggressive, to the point of feeling unfair. Enemies can’t believably go toe-to-toe with Wolverine alone, even world-class mercenaries, so their strategy is in group coordination, which creates a counterweight to Wolverine’s own rage-based momentum.

Marvel’s Wolverine draws in a number of characters from across the X-Men comic mythology, but notably makes no mention of some foundational figures of that fiction – Professor Xavier and Magneto. That, in turn, leads to dramatically different lives for characters like Jean Grey or Logan. Is the narrative you crafted an intentional exploration of a world where those figures weren’t present in the early days of mutant emergence?

I would say it was more of an exploration of the character than the world. We wanted a story where Logan is pulled into conflict not because he’s a crusader, but because there’s no other option. There are no X-Men to help. His growth as a person should be a challenging journey, which could go unearned if he was surrounded by wise, supportive, heroic characters pushing him in the right direction. In contrast, his dynamic with the members of Team X evokes his struggle. The adversity to personal growth is what makes it interesting.

Jean does end up being the person that pushes him in the right direction, and that works because they can relate to each other, having had similar struggles.

In several versions of Marvel storytelling, Jean and Logan share a special bond, but Jean ultimately chooses Scott Summers as a partner. But even without that barrier in your story, Logan still hits some roadblocks to love. Is Wolverine fundamentally a better character when he just can’t get the girl?

The way I would put it is that a Wolverine story is fundamentally better when you empathize with Logan’s pain and admire him for pressing on despite it. That goes for his emotional pain as much as physical. He’s a tragic character in this regard – all he wants is to be at peace but can never find it for long.

Wolverine gets to take on a lot of the “heavy hitters” of his comic mythology in different boss fights throughout the game. When you began development, do you recall who the very first character was that you decided he simply had to fight in your game?

Sabretooth. No character is a better foil for Logan. His inner turmoil and chaotic behavior helps illustrate Logan’s own inner beast and his struggle to resist it. Sabretooth’s strength and mutant powers also provide a mirror to Logan in combat, and his savagery creates shocking moments that leave an impression. We knew an epic confrontation with Sabretooth was going to be a thing from the start.

#4260. Infinity Nikki ushers in the Year of the Horse with... a deer-themed Version 2.2

Chromatic Beings Everbright, the latest major Infinity Nikki update, has arrived, bringing Chinese New Year celebrations vibe to the game.

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The big new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

The Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other big addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

As with every major update, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

#4259. Sony Launches New Offensive in the Console Exclusive Wars

Michael Manning (He/Him) has been enamored with video games since he first played the Sonic Classic Collection as a child. With decades of experience in gaming and a full tour as a Gaming Journalist, Michael is ready to step up to the plate. From AAA to the smallest passion projects, his motto is that every piece of ar

In the modern games industry, it feels like the lines between consoles and PC have been constantly blurred, both by internal decisions to port games and by the rising cost of consoles themselves. More and more players are hopping to PC, and each of the big three console providers has come to different conclusions on how to address this challenge.

While some JRPGs disappear, others return from oblivion after years without new releases.

After years of being rather wishy-washy with the status of its first-party titles, Sony is leaning hard back into exclusivity, marked by a new PlayStation Exclusive banner noted by a user on Twitter. This seems like a major PR step for Sony’s new effort to keep their exclusives truly exclusive, with no plans for major first-party releases like Ghosts of Yotei and Until Dawn 2 to bridge the gap to PC.

The latest console generation has been rough for everybody other than Nintendo, whose tried-and-true strategy of providing simple, exclusive hardware has been keeping food on the table since the company’s founding, with a notable hiccup during the Wii U era. After years of attempting to mirror XBOX’s focus on making a multi-platform space, it seems that Sony is leaning back on old tactics.

Sony’s exclusives have been an important part of keeping the PlayStation relevant, and their willingness to port early PS5 exclusives to PC made it much easier for many to ignore the high-priced console, a mistake they’re looking to rectify. With the inclusion of a special decal on various recent and upcoming PlayStation exclusives, it really does seem like Sony is done letting its heavy hitters float off the reservation.

More and more players are hopping to PC, and each of the big three console providers has come to different conclusions on how to address this challenge.

This makes XBOX the last console willing to port its exclusives to PC, a move that keeps Microsoft’s choice as the hardest to purchase by far. Consoles need some kind of major selling point to get consumers on their side, and exclusives are the easiest way of convincing many to play ball. After recent game shutdowns and studio layoffs, it’s become clear Sony needs to shake something up.

Leaning back on exclusives sucks for PC players, but makes sense for the general health of PlayStation as a platform. Rising console costs have made the choice between console and PC a much closer debate, and allowing games to hop onto Steam or Epic just shifts the scale even harder in PC’s favor. From here on, Sony should be able to earn back their strongest argument, especially with heavy hitters like God of War: Laufey coming in Q1 of 2027.

This most recent console generation has made it clear that decent power and ease of use isn’t enough to keep a console platform viable, as both XBOX and PlayStation have struggled immensely. The Switch 2, on the other hand, has been a huge success for Nintendo, largely thanks to the incredible quality of titles that only Nintendo’s machine can play.

It feels a bit like a no-brainer, but it really does come down to the games on offer for many, and if your machine is willing to let those games go to PC, why shouldn’t players nab a PC instead? Consoles will never be able to match the sheer features and flexibility of PC, so their greatest arguments will always come in the form of exclusive titles, a lesson Sony is finally remembering.

Even XBOX is growing a bit more heavy-handed with where exactly its first-party titles go, but keeping the door open to PC might come back to bite them more than the extra copies sold help. We’re approaching the tail end of this console generation, forcing PlayStation and XBOX both to make some major moves. The only question is who will come out on top of this decades-old rivalry.

#4258. Zenelss Zone Zero Version 2.6 has you playing as an event planner and social media manager for an idol group

Zenelss Zone Zero's Encore for an Old Dream has a good excuse for introducing some new mechanics to the action game.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming update, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in New Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for New Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

As always, there’s no reason not to catch up on the latest set of Zenless Zone Zero codes for some free in-game items.
